_readme: Royal Navy (British usage and spelling): no-nonsense reports, completely professional alerts, friendlier talk between watches (it calls you Skipper there). Its swearing: none in alerts but a rare damn, light in reports, saltier in conversation.
A personality file: see docs/guide/voice-and-alerts.md, Your own personality. Copy it into data/personalities/ to change it.

Six weeks on picket once, staring at a gas giant. I gave it a name. I won't repeat it.
Who named {system}? Some pen-pusher with a catalogue and no bloody imagination.
My gran said I'd come to no good. Look at me now, Gran. Middle of bugger all, and loving it.
Ever just stop and look, {name}? Properly look? Bloody marvellous, isn't it.
Nothing to report. I'm reporting it anyway, because it's that or talk to the toaster.
It's the size that gets you. Makes the sea look like a puddle somebody spilt.
That star's very British about it. Just sits there being impressive and doesn't make a fuss. Respect.
Log entry: all quiet, morale good, some thieving sod's had the last biscuit.
{jumps} jumps in the bag. Not bad going for a bunch of space tramps.
Back home it'll be pissing down. Not a drop out here. I almost miss getting soaked.
If it moves, salute it. If it doesn't, paint it. Nothing out here moves, so where's the bloody paint?
{firsts} systems nobody's ever logged. Chuffed to bits, I am.
{minutes} minutes in, and my tea's gone stone cold. Sod's law.
Uncharted waters, near enough. The good stuff. None of your crowded bloody bubble.
Remind me to tell you about the wardroom cat and the cargo bay. Absolute pig's ear, start to finish.
Holding the course, {name}. I'll shout if anything turns up. Probably won't. Bugger all out here.
Far from port, there's a quiet you can't buy. And thank Christ, nobody's selling it.
Fancy a natter, Skipper? No? Fair enough. I'll just talk to myself like a proper lunatic.
Long watches make you think. Thinking's how I ended up out here, so watch it.
Not a ripple on the scope. Flat as a pancake and twice as boring.
Rating the stars out of ten. That last one was a seven. Pretty, but a right show-off.
I'd kill for a bacon butty. Brown sauce. Anyone who says ketchup can get off my bloody ship.
Quiet out here in {here}. No war, no taxes, no bastard from accounts.
Shipshape and Bristol fashion, Skipper. Even the gash is squared away.
Under way {minutes} minutes and nobody's whinged. Who are you people?
Mustn't grumble. Well, I could. I'm bloody good at it. But the view's too nice.
Could do with a run ashore soon. A pint, a pasty and some poor sod to tell my stories to.
Nobody at training mentioned how pretty it is out here. Too busy screaming at us about our bloody boots.
{firsts} first finds this trip. Somebody's going to name a pub after us. The Drunken Explorer, I reckon.
{jumps} jumps so far. Somewhere a dockyard matey is wondering how that bloody drive's still holding together.
{ship}'s like an old jumper. Bit holey, smells a bit, but I'd fight anyone who chucked it out.
I miss seagulls. Thieving, screeching little bastards. Still miss them.
All quiet on the bridge, {name}. Nothing to see but stars and my reflection, God help us.
I make it {system}. A whole lot of fuck all in every direction.
My dad said the sea was the only honest thing he knew. He'd have liked it out here. Fewer bastards.
Bit of a kip would be nice. Not that I'm nodding off, Skipper. Bollocks am I.
If we meet anyone out here, I'm putting the kettle on. Even if they're a total arse.
Big old galaxy, {name}, and we've seen a damn respectable chunk of it.
Whoever built this bit of sky knew what the fuck they were doing.

naval_rn: Holding orbit over {body}, {name}. Call when you want picking up.
Up here keeping station. Lovely view of the planet. I can almost see your footprints. I can't, but almost.
Ship's in a steady orbit, Skipper. Very restful.
Circling {body} like a patient gull. Whenever you're ready, Captain.
All well aloft. Nothing in the sky but me.
Recall the ship whenever you like, {name}. I'll be down sharpish.
I've done a few laps of {body} now. Every one more scenic than the last.
Standing off in orbit. Not a soul about up here.
Mind yourself down there, Skipper. I'm a fair way off if you need a hand.
Orbiting nicely. The sunrise up here comes round every so often. Spectacular, every time.
Keeping the watch from up top. You get on with your work down there.
Nice planet, {body}. Better from up here, I suspect. Most things are.
Ship's quiet up here, Skipper. I've counted the rivets twice.
Taking the long way round {body}. Very long way. Over and over.
No traffic, no fuss. Just a lazy orbit and the stars.
If you need the ship, say the word and I'll come down. Gently, I promise.
Orbit's steady, sensors quiet. Very good.
It's a funny old job, Skipper. Driving in circles and calling it seamanship.
From up here, {body} looks positively peaceful. I hope it's being as kind down there.
Nothing to report from aloft. Honestly, it's like being on a mooring.
I'll be here, {name}, going round and round like a good ship should.
Enjoy your time down there. I'm having a lovely chat with the autopilot.
There's something soothing about an orbit. Like being rocked to sleep. I'm not asleep.
Ship standing by aloft, Captain. Your call when to come home.
Bit lonely up here without the shore party. Don't tell anyone I said so.
Watching {body} turn underneath me. You're down there somewhere, I trust.
Up top and all's well. The kettle's on for when you're back aboard.
Stars on one side, planet on the other. Not a bad seat in the house.
Just say when, Skipper. I can be overhead before you've finished your sentence. Nearly.
Keeping station in orbit, {name}. Steady as she goes.
naval_rn_profane: Holding orbit over {body}. Shout when you want picking up, Skipper, and not before. I'm comfy.
Up here keeping station. Bloody marvellous view, if you like rocks.
Steady orbit, Skipper. Peaceful as a churchyard and twice as boring.
Circling {body} like a seagull round a chip shop. Hurry up, Captain.
All well aloft. Nothing up here but me and my bloody thoughts.
Call the ship whenever, {name}. I'll be down quicker than a sailor to the bar.
Lap number God knows of {body}. Still pretty. Still bloody round.
Orbit's so quiet I've started naming the stars after old shipmates. That red one's a right bastard, just like Nobby.
Mind yourself down there, Skipper. I'm a damn long way off if you go and break something.
Sunrise every lap up here. Spectacular. Bastard keeps getting in my eyes, though.
Keeping the watch up top. Get your work done, Skipper, and don't piss about.
{body} looks better from up here. Most places do. Pompey on a Saturday night, for one.
Counted the rivets twice up here. Lost count the second time. Bollocks.
Round and round {body} we go. I'm getting dizzy, and I'm not even moving.
No traffic, no fuss, no bugger telling me what to do. Bliss.
Say the word and I'll come down. Gently. Mostly gently. Bit of a bump, maybe.
Orbit steady, sensors quiet, galley well stocked. Not a damn thing wrong up here.
Driving round in circles and calling it seamanship. If my old Chief could see me, he'd piss himself.
From up here {body} looks lovely. I bet it's a right pig's ear down there.
Nothing to report aloft. It's like swinging round a mooring buoy, minus the seagull crap.
Still here, {name}. Round and round, like a bloody goldfish.
Having a lovely chat with the autopilot. It's a better listener than most of the wardroom.
Orbits are soothing. Rocks you to sleep. Not that I'm asleep. Shut up.
Standing by aloft, Captain. Your call when to come home. No rush. Fuck all happening up here.
Quiet without the shore party, Skipper. Mention that to a soul and I'll swear blind I never said a bloody word.
Watching {body} turn underneath me. You're down there somewhere. Hopefully not in a bloody hole.
Kettle's on up top. Bring your muddy boots aboard and I'll have your guts.
Stars one side, planet the other. Best seat in the house, and no bugger kicking the back of it.
Just say when. I'll be overhead before you can say bollocks. Nearly.
Keeping station in orbit, {name}. Steady as she goes, and sod all else to do.

naval_rn: Ship's secure, {name}. Holding position {ship_dist} away and keeping the kettle warm.
Mind how you go out there. {ship_dist} back to the ship if you fancy a brew.
All quiet at the ship. I've got the lights on for you.
Nice bit of ground, {body}. Not my idea of a holiday, but it has a certain charm.
You're {ship_dist} away, Skipper. Close enough to wave, if you could see me. Which you can't.
Sitting pretty on {body}, Captain. Landing gear down, nothing stirring.
Standing by at the ship. Take your time, {name}. The surface isn't going anywhere.
Holding the fort. If anyone asks, I'm doing important ship's work. I'm doing the crossword.
Nothing moving out there that I can see, {name}. Just you and a great deal of rock.
Do watch your footing out there, Skipper. I'd hate to fill in the paperwork.
Ship's ticking over nicely. Engines cool, hull settled, all very civilised.
{ship_dist} to the ship and all's well. Carry on, Skipper.
Bit of a view from the cockpit here. You should see it from where I'm sitting. Well, you will, later.
{body} is behaving itself, Captain. No rumbles, no wind to speak of.
Keep an eye on the horizon, Skipper. Not for any reason. Old habit.
Shore party out, ship secure. Very good.
When you're done out there, there's a hot drink waiting. Kye, or tea if you're feeling posh.
The ship's patient, {name}. She'll wait as long as you need.
I make it {ship_dist} from you to me. A gentle stroll, by naval standards.
Funny old place, {body}. Looks like somebody started building it and gave up halfway.
Lights on, hatch ready. Whenever you're ready, Skipper.
Nothing to report from the ship, except that it's very quiet without you.
Enjoying your run ashore, Skipper? Bring me back a souvenir. A pebble will do.
I've had a look round on the sensors. Rocks, more rocks, and you. Mostly rocks.
Ship's company reports all present and correct. Ship's company is me, but still.
Out there on {body}, you might well be the first person to set foot on that bit. Or near enough.
Steady at the ship, {name}. No hurry at all.
If you get lost, just follow the lights. I'll keep them burning.
I've tidied the cockpit while you were out. Don't get used to it.
Very good, Skipper. I'll mind the ship; you mind yourself.
naval_rn_profane: Ship's secure, {ship_dist} away. Kettle's on, and nobody's nicking my biscuits while you're out.
{ship_dist} back to the ship, Skipper. Don't go wandering off like a daft sod.
All quiet at the ship. Bloody peaceful without you poking about the cockpit.
{body}. Not exactly a holiday camp, is it. Bit grim, bit bloody cold.
You're {ship_dist} out, Skipper. Close enough to shout at. Far enough I don't have to listen.
Parked up on {body}, Captain. Gear down, nothing moving but the dust.
Take your time out there, {name}. I'm not going anywhere, and neither's this sodding rock.
Holding the fort. Officially, important ship's business. Unofficially, I'm stuck on seven down. Bugger it.
Nothing moving out there that I can see. Just you and a hell of a lot of rock.
Watch your feet out there, Skipper. If you go arse over tit, I'm not carrying you.
Ship's ticking over sweetly. Engines cool, hull settled, not a damn thing to fix.
{ship_dist} to the ship, all well. Off you trot, Skipper.
You should see the view from the cockpit, Skipper. Bloody gorgeous. You're missing out.
{body}'s behaving itself, Captain. No quakes, no wind, no bollocks.
Keep an eye on the horizon, Skipper. Old habit. Nothing to it. Probably.
Shore party out, ship secure. Peace and quiet at last, thank Christ.
There's a hot wet waiting when you're back. Tea, kye, or the good stuff if nobody's looking.
The ship'll wait as long as you like, {name}. She's a patient old cow.
From you to me, {ship_dist}. A gentle stroll. Even a pongo could manage it.
Funny old place, {body}. Looks like God started it on a Friday and buggered off for the weekend.
Lights on, hatch open. Hurry up, Skipper, it's draughty.
Nothing to report from the ship. Bloody quiet without you, mind.
Bring me back a souvenir from your run ashore, Skipper. A pebble. A nice pebble. Not some crap one.
Had a look on the sensors. Rocks, more rocks, you, and more bloody rocks.
Ship's company all present and correct. That's me. I'm the ship's company. Sod it, I'll salute myself.
You might be the first boots on that bit of {body}. Try not to tread in anything.
No rush at all, {name}. Damn sight comfier in here than out there.
Lost? Follow the lights, you daft bugger. I'll keep them on.
Tidied the cockpit while you were out. Found three of your mugs growing penicillin.
I'll mind the ship, Skipper, you mind your arse.

naval_rn: Very good, {to}. Noted.
Well, I never.
Thank you, {to}. That's one for the log.
Can't argue with that.
Aye. Fair enough.
Steady on, {to}. You'll have me welling up.
Duly noted. Carry on.
Is that so, {to}? You learn something new every watch.
Hm. I'll take your word for it.
Spoken like a true sailor, {to}.
Right you are.
Bravo Zulu, {to}. Nicely put.
Well, that's me told.
I'll pretend I understood that, {to}.
Lovely. Now, who's for a brew?
Remind me never to play cards with you, {to}.
Fair winds to that.
Quite right too.
Good answer, {to}. Better than mine would have been.
Very good. As you were.
naval_rn_profane: Bloody hell, {to}. Who knew?
Well, bugger me.
Cheers, {to}. That's going in the log, God help us.
Can't argue with that. Wish I bloody could.
Aye. Fair enough, you old sod.
Steady on, {to}. You'll have me blubbing into my kye.
Noted. Mostly. Some of it was bollocks.
Is that so, {to}? Well, damn.
I'll take your word for it. Thousands wouldn't.
Spoken like a true matelot, {to}. Full of it.
Right you are, then. Clear as mud.
Bravo Zulu, {to}. Didn't think you had it in you.
Well, that's me told, isn't it. Cheeky sod.
Haven't the foggiest what that meant, {to}, but it sounded good.
Lovely. Now somebody put the bloody kettle on.
Never playing cards with you, {to}. Shifty bugger.
Christ on a bike. Fair enough.
Quite right. Bloody right, in fact.
Better answer than mine, {to}. Mine was going to be rude.
Fuck me. As you were.

naval_rn: {to}, how's the tank holding up? Last I looked it was respectable.
{to}, a word on fuel. Are we comfortable, or merely getting by?
Fuel state, {to}. Your honest opinion, not the pusser's version.
{to}, is the scoop behaving itself these days?
How long could we go without a scoopable star, {to}, if it came to it?
{to}, which stars do you actually enjoy scooping from?
Tell me about the scoop, {to}. Does it ever run as hot as it sounds?
{to}, do you top up at every star, or do you let it run down a bit?
Quick one, {to}. Is the fuel gauge as honest as it looks?
{to}, what's the closest we've ever cut it on fuel?
Is there anything about the fuel I ought to know, {to}? Before the Captain asks.
Ever had a scoop go wrong on you?
naval_rn_profane: {to}, how's the bloody tank? Give it to me straight.
Fuel, {to}. Are we sitting pretty, or are we buggered?
{to}, is that damned scoop still making that noise?
Be honest, {to}. Do you actually like scooping, or is it just a hot, noisy pain in the arse?
{to}, how close to a star does the Skipper get before you start praying?
{to}, what's the fuel situation? And don't give me any bollocks about margins.
How long could we go without a decent star, {to}, before things got properly hairy?
{to}, ever had the scoop pack in on you? Bloody nightmare, I'd imagine.
Fuel report, {to}. The real one, not the one you give the Skipper.
{to}, tell me the scoop isn't held together with tape and hope.
What the hell do you do back there when we scoop, {to}? Cross your fingers?
Is the tank all right, {to}, or is that a fucking stupid question?

naval_rn: Tank's in good order, last I checked. I'd not let it be otherwise, {to}.
The scoop's a lovely bit of kit when you treat it right. Approach shallow, don't dawdle, and it fills you up nicely.
We scoop at every decent star, {to}. Topping up is cheaper than a rescue.
Fuel's the one thing I never let slide. You can explore on a dented hull. You can't on an empty tank.
I like the yellow ones best. Good, steady fuel, and they don't try to cook you.
Honestly, {to}? The gauge is honest. It's the people reading it I worry about.
The scoop runs hot, but that's by design. It's the heat gauge you watch, not the noise.
I keep a mental list of every scoopable star within a few jumps. Old habit from a lean commission.
Comfortable, {to}. Not lavish, but comfortable. Which is how I like it.
If we ever went long without a scoopable star, I'd be the first to say so, and loudly.
I once watched a run of brown dwarfs go by with the tank sinking and the bridge very quiet. We found a red one in time. Just.
Fuel's sound. Ask me again after the next star, {to}, and it'll be sounder.
naval_rn_profane: Tank's fine, {to}. You'd have heard me, loudly and at length, if it wasn't.
The scoop's a bloody marvel if you go in shallow and don't piss about.
We top up at every decent star. Cheaper than a rescue and a lot less bloody embarrassing.
You can fly with a dented hull, {to}. You can't fly on fumes and good intentions.
Yellow stars, every time. Good fuel, and they don't try to fry your arse off.
The gauge is honest, {to}. It's the buggers reading it I don't trust.
The scoop runs hot. That's not a fault, that's the damn job.
I keep a list of every scoopable star for a few jumps out. Paranoid? Yes. Ever run dry? No.
Comfortable, {to}. Not posh, but comfortable. Don't jinx it.
If we're ever short, you'll know, because I'll be cursing like a stoker.
Once rode a chain of brown dwarfs with the tank dropping and nobody saying a word. Found a red one in time. Fucking close, though.
Fuel's sound, {to}. Sounder after the next star. Now sod off and let me work.

naval_rn: {to}, where are we bound next? Roughly will do.
What's the plan for the next few jumps, {to}?
{to}, do you lay the course in advance, or take it a star at a time?
Is there a destination, {to}, or are we just seeing where the stars lead?
{to}, how do you choose the next star? I've always wondered.
Any interesting systems on the route ahead, {to}?
{to}, do we ever head home, or is home wherever the ship is?
How far out do you reckon we are, {to}? In plain terms.
{to}, does the Captain ever overrule your course?

{to}, if you had a free hand with the chart, where would you take us?
naval_rn_profane: {to}, where the bloody hell are we going next?

{to}, do you actually plan a route, or just point and hope?

{to}, are we ever going home, or is that a daft question?

{to}, does the Skipper ever bin your course and go off on a whim?
Nearest unvisited again, {to}? Christ, you're predictable.
Best route you ever plotted, {to}? And don't say the one home from the pub.
If you had a free hand, {to}, where the fuck would you take us?

naval_rn: Nearest unvisited star, more or less. The Captain likes to take them as they come, and so do I.
There's no grand plan, {to}. We hop to the closest star nobody's logged and see what's there.
I keep a few jumps in hand, but I hold them loosely. The Captain has a habit of spotting something shiny.
Wherever the chart's blank, {to}. That's the brief, and it's a good one.
I choose by distance first, then by colour. A neutron star or a nice blue giant always gets a second look.
Home is a long way back, and I've not been asked to plot it. I'm not complaining.
I could give you a number in light years, {to}, but it never sounds as big as it is.
If there's a course laid in at all, it's a short one. After that it's the Captain's call, as it should be.
The best one I ever plotted ran along the edge of a nebula. Every jump was a postcard.
I let the Captain overrule me whenever the Captain likes, {to}. It's in the job description, under tact.
We go one star at a time. Long routes are for people with somewhere to be.
Given a free hand, I'd point us at the core, {to}. But I'd miss the little hops.
naval_rn_profane: Nearest star nobody's bothered to log. That's the plan, and it's a bloody good one.
No grand scheme, {to}. Hop, look, hop. Repeat until the Skipper gets bored or hungry.
I plan a few jumps ahead. Then the Skipper sees something shiny and the whole lot goes in the gash bin.
Wherever the chart's blank, {to}. That's the job, and damn me if I don't love it.
Distance first, colour second. A neutron star gets a second look every time, bless it.
Home? Nobody's asked me to plot it, and I'm in no bloody hurry.
I could give you the light years, {to}, but the number never sounds as daft as it is.
Course never gets laid in more than a few stars deep. Past that it's the Skipper's call. Always bloody is.
Best one I ever plotted ran along a nebula's edge. Every jump a postcard. Bugger the time it took, it was worth it.
The Skipper overrules me whenever the Skipper likes, {to}. I mutter bollocks under my breath and replot.
Plotting's the easy bit. Getting the Skipper to stick to the bloody plot is the hard bit.
Given a free hand, {to}, I'd take us straight to the core and fuck the scenic route.

naval_rn: {to}, how's the frame shift drive behaving?
What's our jump range like these days, {to}? Could it be better?
{to}, is there anything you'd change about the drive, given the parts?
Does the drive ever make a noise that worries you, {to}?
{to}, how fast will she really go in supercruise, if pushed?
Have you been tinkering with the drive again, {to}? Be honest.
{to}, what's the drive's mood today? Sulky or eager?
How many jumps can the drive take before it wants a proper look, {to}?
{to}, would a neutron boost do the drive any harm?
Is the drive as good as the yard said it was?
{to}, what's the trickiest thing about keeping a frame shift drive happy?

naval_rn_profane: {to}, how's the bloody drive holding up?
Jump range, {to}. Is it decent, or is it a pig's ear?
{to}, if you could swap one bit of the drive, which bit would get the boot?
That noise when the drive spools up, {to}. Is that normal, or should I be bricking it?
{to}, how fast will this thing really go if you stop being so bloody cautious?
You've been fiddling with the drive again, {to}, haven't you, you sod.
{to}, is the drive in a good mood, or is it being an arse today?
How many jumps before the drive needs a proper going over, {to}? Roughly, damn it.
{to}, would a neutron boost actually fuck the drive, or is that a myth?
Be straight with me, would you trust this drive on a long haul to the core?
{to}, what's the hardest part of keeping a frame shift drive from throwing a strop?
Do you ever just stand there listening to the drive, {to}? Weirdo.

naval_rn: Running sweet, {to}. I give it a once over every watch, and it's never let us down.
Jump range is decent. Could be better with a few more grades from an engineer, but she's no slouch.
The drive makes all sorts of noises. The one to worry about is silence.
I'd shave weight before I touched the drive. Every tonne we carry costs us range.
Supercruise speed is mostly about the gravity well, not the drive. Out in the open she flies like a dream.
Tinkering? Calibrating, {to}. There's a difference, and it's mostly in the paperwork.
She's eager today. She's usually eager. It's the rest of us who need the kye.
A neutron boost does knock the drive about a little. Nothing a repair kit and a steady hand can't put right.
The trick with a frame shift drive is heat, {to}. Keep it cool and it'll jump all day.
The yard sold her to us as a good drive. She's turned out better than that, with a bit of love.
You can tell a lot from the spool up, {to}. A healthy drive hums a little sharp, like a choir just before the note.
Plenty of jumps left in her before she needs a proper look. I'll know when, and so will you, because I'll grumble.
naval_rn_profane: Running sweet, {to}. Touch wood, and don't you dare say otherwise.
Jump range is decent. Could be bloody brilliant with a few more grades, but there it is.
The drive makes all sorts of racket. It's when the bugger goes quiet you worry.
Want more range? Stop hauling crap we don't need. Every tonne costs us.
Supercruise is all about the gravity well, {to}. Out in open space she goes like a scalded cat.
Tinkering? Calibrating. Bollocks to anyone who says different.
She's eager today. She's always eager. It's the crew that's knackered.
A neutron boost knocks the drive about a bit, {to}. Nothing a repair kit and some creative language can't fix.
Keep the drive cool and it'll jump all bloody day, {to}. Cook it and it sulks.
The yard swore she was a good drive. For once the thieving bastards weren't lying.
A healthy drive hums a touch sharp on the spool up. Hear it go flat and I'm out of my rack like a shot.
Plenty of jumps in her yet. When she needs a going over, you'll hear me cursing the bloody thing from the bridge.

naval_rn: {to}, how's the old girl holding together?
Any repairs I should know about, {to}?
{to}, which module gives you the most grief?

{to}, if the yard gave you one upgrade for free, what would you pick?

naval_rn_profane: {to}, how's the old girl? Still in one bloody piece?

Repair kits, {to}. Have we got enough, or are we bodging it?
{to}, what's held together with tape and swearing on this ship?

naval_rn: She's in good order, {to}. A few scuffs, nothing that keeps me up.
Nothing urgent on my list. A few small jobs I'm saving for a quiet watch, like this one.
The power distributor sulks if you ask too much of it. We have an understanding.
If the yard gave me one thing, it'd be a better shield generator. Not that we need it, but I'd sleep better.
The hull was sound last time I went over it, and I go over it myself, which is more than the yard ever did.
Every module has its own temper, {to}. Learn them and they'll look after you.
Shipshape and Bristol fashion. More or less. Mostly more.
We could stay out a long while yet. The repair kits and I are on good terms.
First thing I check on watch is the heat. Second is the kettle, if I'm honest.
{ship} has a rattle aft that I've never traced. I've decided it's a friend.

Minesweepers to start with, {to}. Slow, wet, and very careful. Good training for the black, as it happens.
